newsitem.title: INDIA: ANZ bank awarded $240mln in India dispute.
newsitem.headline: ANZ bank awarded $240mln in India dispute.

text.p: ANZ Grindlays Bank was awarded $240 million by an Indian arbitration panel for money forfeited by the bank in the wake of a share scandal that rocked the country's stock markets in 1992, a senior official of the bank said on Sunday.
The National Housing Bank (NHB), a wholly owned subsidiary India's central bank, was ordered to repay ANZ Grindlays the money by the three-member panel, which met at a Bombay hotel on Saturday.

"The claim of NHB against Grindlays has been dismissed and it has been asked to repay the disputed amount. We will have to wait for the implementation of the arbitration panel's order," Mehli M Mistri, chief executive officer of ANZ Grindlays told Reuters.
The award is linked to transactions involving Harshad Mehta, the broker at the centre of the 1992 bull market which exploded in scandal, Indian financial dailies reported.
NHB, in 1992, issued nine crossed account payee only cheques favouring ANZ Grindlays, which Grindlays credited to Mehta's account.
ANZ Grindlays was told by the the Reserve Bank of India to repay the money to the NHB as it sought to unravel Mehta's dealings.
The foreign bank disputed NHB's claim, but agreed to comply with the RBI's instruction subject to the case being referred to an arbitration panel.
The panel ordered that NHB repay ANZ Grindlays 5.06 billion rupees, plus interest from 1992. The Financial Express newspaper estimated the total award at around 8.6 billion rupees ($240 million).
Mehli said he had not read the award yet, but added that the newspapers estimates were reasonably accurate.

The NHB, backed by the RBI, is likely to challenge the panel's decision, first through a special court investigating the 1992 stocks scandal-related transactions and later the Supreme Court, the Financial Express said.
ANZ Grindlays is part of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group.
